biography:
Ernesto José Viso, known as E.J. to the racing world, is a name synonymous with raw aggression and relentless pursuit on the Super Trophy Truck circuit. Born in Caracas, Venezuela, E.J.'s path to motorsports wasn't paved in privilege. His early years were spent tearing through the barrios on a beat-up BMX bike, honing his reflexes and fearlessness. A chance encounter with a local mechanic who moonlighted as a desert racer opened E.J.'s eyes to the world of off-road competition.

Viso's debut in the Super Trophy Trucks was nothing short of explosive. His unyielding style immediately turned heads, earning him both fans and detractors. A defining moment came at the Baja 500, when, despite a blown tire and significant damage to his truck, E.J. refused to concede, pushing his machine beyond its limits to secure a podium finish. That race cemented his reputation as a driver who would fight until the very end.

Now at the peak of his career, E.J. is a force to be reckoned with in every race. While some criticize his aggressive tactics, few can deny his sheer talent and unwavering determination. He's not just racing; he's battling, clawing, and pushing every inch of the way, a true embodiment of the Venezuelan spirit.
drivingStyle: Viso's driving style is best described as 'controlled chaos.' He attacks corners with a ferocity that often borders on recklessness, relying on his lightning-fast reflexes and innate feel for the truck to maintain control. He isn't known for tire management; his philosophy is more akin to 'burn rubber and ask questions later.' While his approach can be risky, it also allows him to gain crucial positions in the early stages of a race. Under pressure, E.J. becomes even more aggressive, often using intimidation tactics to unsettle his rivals.

famousQuote: "I don't race for points; I race for blood. If you're not willing to risk everything, you don't belong on the track."
careerHighlight: Winning the Mint 400 in 2022, overcoming a mechanical failure early in the race to claw his way back to the front and secure a dramatic victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Baja 1000 in 2021, a devastating blow that cost him a potential championship title.
